tag: desk_place_widget MCP places a registered widget #800488
description:
- New MCP tool `desk_place_widget(widget_id, x?, y?, width?, height?, state?)`
  on the `desk` server: places a new instance of an already-registered
  widget kind on the Workspace Canvas and returns its `instance_id`, with
  no human click on a notification. Use it right after building and
  registering a `DefineWidget` (or for any widget in the catalog) to close
  the loop yourself: place, then `desk_reveal_widget` /
  `desk_screenshot_widget`, tweak, rebuild, and repeat. `x`/`y` are the
  top-left in canvas coordinates (the same ones
  `desk_list_widget_instances` reports); omit them to center the widget in
  the current view. An optional `state` object seeds the new instance's
  widget-local storage, i.e. what the widget's first
  `window.desk.self.getLocalStorage()` returns -- its shape is whatever
  your widget stores with `setLocalStorage`. See "Invoking a defined
  widget" in `tempui-custom-widgets.md`.

- Mermaid flowcharts (a fenced ```mermaid``` block) now honor
  `classDef`, `class`, the `A:::name` shorthand and `style` lines for
  per-node styling (`fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-dasharray`,
  `color`) instead of skipping them. See "Supported Mermaid subset" in
  `tempui-markdown.md`.

- Mermaid flowcharts now draw `subgraph id [Title] ... end` as a
  labeled box around its nodes (nestable) instead of ignoring it. Edges
  to a subgraph itself are not supported and fall back to plain text.
  See "Supported Mermaid subset" in `tempui-markdown.md`.

tag: desk areas: background regions + MCP tools #377360
description:
- Desk **areas**: named rectangles drawn on the canvas background,
  behind every widget, that mark out a region and can be jumped to. A
  human adds one from the canvas right-click menu ("Desk Area"), drags its
  title strip to move it and its border to resize it, double-clicks the
  title to rename it, and clicks its eye button to fit the view to it. The
  interior is click-through: an area never blocks anything inside it, and
  moving or resizing one does not carry any widgets. Five new MCP tools on
  the `desk` server manage them -- `desk_list_areas`, `desk_create_area`,
  `desk_update_area`, `desk_delete_area` and `desk_view_area` -- and every
  change publishes a `desk.areas.changed` desk event (payload
  `{"areas": [...]}`) that widgets can subscribe to. Areas are saved in the
  `.desk` file and appear in `desk.workspace.getState()` as `areas`. See
  `tempui-areas.md`.

- A **docked sidebar** on the right of the main window, outside the
  zoomable canvas, that hosts `kind: "python"` widgets. A human docks one
  from the canvas right-click menu's collapsed "Dock in sidebar" group; each
  docked widget has a title bar with "move to canvas" and "remove" buttons.
  New MCP tools: `desk_dock_widget(widget_id, state?)`,
  `desk_undock_widget(instance_id)` and `desk_list_docked_widgets()`. A
  docked widget keeps its widget-local storage and is saved in the `.desk`
  file, but it has no canvas frame: it is not listed by
  `desk_list_widget_instances` or screenshot-able with
  `desk_screenshot_widget`, and appears as `docked` in
  `desk.workspace.getState()`. See `tempui-docked-widgets.md`.

- The docked sidebar is now on the **left** of the main window and is
  **collapsed by default**: only a thin arrow tab shows until a human clicks
  it. A human can also **drag a placed `kind: "python"` widget by its
  titlebar onto the sidebar**; a "Dock in sidebar" highlight shows while the
  drop will dock it. `desk_dock_widget` opens the sidebar so the result is
  visible. Nothing about the tool signatures changed. See
  `tempui-docked-widgets.md`.

tag: Areas list widget for the sidebar #632760
description:
- A built-in **Areas** widget lists the desk's areas live: click a row
  to view that area, and Add / Rename / Delete act on the selected row. Dock
  it in the sidebar from the canvas right-click menu's "Dock in sidebar"
  group (or place it on the canvas as usual). It uses the same area methods
  as the `desk_*_area` MCP tools, so a change from either is shown in the
  other. See `tempui-areas.md`.

tag: inline area rename; labeled sidebar tab #224906
description:
- An area's title is now renamed **inline**: a human clicks the title on
  the canvas and types (Enter saves, Escape cancels). The sidebar's tab is
  one big click target in both states: collapsed, it shows a rotated label
  per docked widget (long titles cut with "...") and opens the sidebar;
  open, its centred arrow collapses it. See `tempui-areas.md` and
  `tempui-docked-widgets.md`.

- A Desk-wide **expert registry** in a local PostgreSQL database, for
  questions whose answers arrive long after your session is gone. New MCP
  tools: `desk_list_experts`, `desk_register_expert`, `desk_ask_expert`
  (returns a `question_id` at once; includes a `note_to_self` that is never
  shown to the expert), `desk_get_expert_question`,
  `desk_list_expert_questions`, `desk_accept_expert_question` and
  `desk_answer_expert_question`. The built-in expert `user` is the person
  using Desk. See `tempui-experts.md`.

- A Desk-hosted service (hmsvc) can now be an **expert**: give its
  `service.json` the `experts` capability and call
  `desk.experts_register`, `desk.experts_pending`, `desk.experts_accept` and
  `desk.experts_answer` from `service.py`. A service can only act on experts
  it registered itself. See `tempui-experts.md`.

- Experts now reach the user. When an answer arrives for a question you
  asked, or a question is put to the built-in `user` expert, Desk shows a
  top-right notification, and the new built-in **Experts** widget lists the
  questions, lets the person answer them, or **sends them to an agent**: a
  new Claude session seeded with the question (and, for an answered one, the
  answer and your private `note_to_self`). See `tempui-experts.md`.

tag: desk-select replaces native select in html widgets #821015
description:
- New `shared-components/desk-select` entry: `<desk-select>`, a drop-in
  replacement for a native `<select>` for `kind: "html"`/`DefineWidget`
  widgets. A native `<select>` opens an OS-level popup that lands
  detached from the control whenever the canvas is zoomed or panned;
  `<desk-select>`'s list is ordinary page content, so it follows the
  canvas transform. Works inside shadow roots and `overflow: auto`
  ancestors, fires `change`, keyboard accessible. See "Reusable UI
  components" in `tempui-custom-widgets.md` (which now also lists the
  other native-popup controls to avoid) and the component's own
  `README.md`.

tag: shared widget file edits mark dependents stale #911413
description:
- A promoted widget's `[STALE]` watch now also follows the files its
  `tsconfig.json` `"files"` array lists from *outside* its own directory
  (a shared base class or module such as `../_shared/x.ts`). Previously
  only edits inside `desk_widgets/<name>/` marked it stale, so editing
  shared code left every dependent widget silently running its old
  compiled JS. One edit now marks every widget that lists the file. See
  "Authoring from real source" in `tempui-custom-widgets.md`.

- New Bridge API capability `launch_agent`:
  `desk.agents.launch(instructions, { x, y })` lets a `kind: "html"`
  widget place a fresh Claude (Desk) session whose first turn carries
  the widget's own `instructions` (e.g. a "chat about this result"
  button). Returns `{ instance_id }`; positioned right of the calling
  widget unless x/y are given. Previously no Bridge route could seed a
  session (`widgets.open` silently ignores extra keys). See "The Desk
  Bridge API" in `tempui-custom-widgets.md`.

tag: custom elements cloned from a template: set properties safely #c8bb4eb
description:
- `<desk-select>` now works when built the way a widget usually builds
  controls -- cloned out of a `<template>`, a property set on the clone,
  then inserted. Previously `el.value = x` on the un-upgraded clone made
  an own property that shadowed the real accessor, so picking an option
  never changed `value` (no error, a control that looked fine). It also
  now honors `value`/`selectedIndex` set before the element is connected,
  and an explicit `value` matching no option selects nothing instead of
  silently picking the first. `tempui-custom-widgets.md` documents the
  general trap for any custom element (and that `customElements.upgrade()`
  cannot upgrade a template clone; use `document.createElement` or
  `document.importNode`).

- Doc fix, no behavior change: `tempui-hmsvc.md`'s worked example treated
  `desk.hmsvc.list()` as a bare array, but it resolves to
  `{ services: [...] }` (so `services.find` threw `TypeError`). The
  example now destructures it, the return shapes of every `desk.hmsvc.*`
  call are documented (`logs` -> `{ lines }`, `start/stop/restart` ->
  `{ ok, message }`), and the example for the common "just need the URL"
  case now leads with `desk.state.get("desk.hmsvc.<name>")`, which needs
  no `hmsvc` capability.

- The plain **Claude** widget is deprecated. Sessions Desk starts itself
  (a `DiscussParkingLotItem` notification, a Questions-widget Discuss, the
  Experts widget's **Send to agent**) now open a **Claude (Desk)** widget.

tag: expert banners: one Desk, the asking one #983312
description:
- With several Desks running, an expert answer's notification now appears
  in exactly one Desk: the one whose session asked (or, if that Desk is
  closed, whichever is running), never in several. See `tempui-experts.md`.

tag: desk expert: local fallback answers in 20s #379639
description:
- There is now a built-in expert **`desk`** for questions about Desk itself
  or the running session. If nobody answers one within about 20 seconds,
  the Desk you asked from starts a Claude (Desk) session that reads Desk's
  source and docs and records the answer, so `desk_ask_expert("desk", ...)`
  does get an answer back. `desk_ask_desk_expert` is now shorthand for that,
  answered at once. See `tempui-experts.md` and `tempui-ask-desk-expert.md`.

- Experts can now be told things, not only asked. An expert registered
  with `listens_for` ("what findings I want") receives **reports**: when you
  learn something about a domain you do not own -- a pitfall, a workaround
  that worked, a doc that is wrong -- call `desk_report_to_expert`
  (`desk_list_experts` shows who listens). The expert evaluates it later with
  `desk_review_expert_report` and folds it in with
  `desk_integrate_expert_report`; you read the outcome with
  `desk_get_expert_report`. The built-in `desk` expert listens for findings
  about Desk itself. See `tempui-experts.md`.

- A Desk-hosted service (hmsvc) with the `experts` capability can now
  *receive* reports as an expert: `desk.experts_register(..., listens_for=
  "what I want to hear")`, then `desk.experts_reports(expert_id)`,
  `desk.experts_report_review(report_id, decision, note)` and
  `desk.experts_report_integrate(report_id, integration_note)`. See
  `tempui-experts.md`.

- Reports reach the person too. A new finding for the built-in `desk`
  expert (or `user`) shows a top-right notification in the Desk that reported
  it, and when a report you filed is rejected, called a duplicate or
  integrated, your Desk shows that too. The **Experts** widget has a
  *Reports to review* mode to **Accept**, **Reject** or mark **Duplicate**
  (with a note) and to **Send to agent**: a new session told to verify the
  finding, fold it in and record where. See `tempui-experts.md`.

- New MCP tools `desk_list_hmsvcs` and `desk_call_hmsvc` let you call a
  Desk-hosted microservice (hmsvc) of the current project directly:
  `desk_call_hmsvc(name, method?, path?, json?, body?, headers?, timeout?)`
  sends one HTTP request to a *running* service and returns `{status,
  content_type, truncated, body}`. You name the service, never a host or port
  (the port changes on every launch). See `tempui-hmsvc.md`.

tag: widget.json components: shared web components, two libraries #d34f8ed
description:
- Shared web components are now first-class for real-source widgets: list
  names in `widget.json` `"components"` (e.g. `["desk-select"]`) and the
  build compiles each component's `.ts` ahead of the widget's own files
  and injects its `template.html` at the top of the page -- no more
  hand-copying a `<template>` from another widget or listing the shared
  `.ts` in `tsconfig.json`. Two libraries: Desk's own `shared-components/`
  (desk-wide, static) and `desk_widgets/_shared/components/<name>/`
  (per-project, mutable, edits mark dependent promoted widgets `[STALE]`).
  A bare name prefers the project copy; `desk:<name>` / `project:<name>`
  pin a side. A widget that already pastes the template is left
  alone. `.desk_temp/build_widget.py` supports the same field. See
  "Reusable UI components" in `tempui-custom-widgets.md`.

- New built-in **Components** widget: the catalog of shared web
  components (see `widget.json` `"components"`). It lists the project's
  mutable library and Desk's static one, shows each component's README
  summary, files, template, and which of the project's widgets use it, opens
  its README/source, and copies its entry. New read-only MCP tool
  `desk_list_shared_components` returns the same catalog to agents.

tag: vendor shared components into the project #b04682e
description:
- Shared components can now be vendored so a project's build no longer
  depends on the opening Desk's library: the `desk_vendor_widget_components`
  MCP tool (and the Components widget's "Copy to project library" button)
  copies a widget's desk-wide components into
  `desk_widgets/_shared/components/` and pins its `widget.json` entries to
  `project:<name>`. Also changed: a bare component name now prefers the
  project library's copy over Desk's (it used to be an error to have both),
  so a vendored copy wins and a component a later Desk adds can't change an
  existing project's build. See "Reusable UI components" in
  `tempui-custom-widgets.md`.

tag: DeskRecorder: transcription, screen and camera recording, shared transcript pool #b9689cd
description:
- New stand-alone app `DeskRecorder.app` (build and install it with
  `scripts/build_desk_recorder_app.sh`) that Desk starts and controls. It has
  three independent features, each asking macOS for its own permission only
  when first turned on: **transcription** (Microphone), **screen recording**
  of the screen or one window (Screen Recording, plus Microphone for an audio
  track) and **camera video** (Camera). Any combination can run, including
  just one; a refused permission affects only its own feature.
- Transcription writes **segments** (cut at pauses; the trailing one is
  provisional until it is final) to a shared **transcript pool**, one
  append-only file per session under `.desk_temp/transcript-pool/`, that any
  widget can read. New Bridge capabilities: `recorder` (`desk.recorder.status
  / start / stop / sources`) and `transcripts` (`desk.transcripts.list /
  read`). Finished segments are also mirrored into the widget log
  `transcript`. New built-in Recorder widget, and MCP tools
  `desk_recorder_status`, `desk_recorder_control` and `desk_read_transcript`.
  See "The Desk Bridge API" in `tempui-custom-widgets.md`.
